stays.name: Lake Crackenback Resort & Spa (Oaks)
stays.short_description: 4.5-star alpine resort on 150 acres bordering Kosciuszko National Park, with spa, indoor pool and direct access to Skitube.
stays.long_description: Nestled in the Thredbo Valley on the banks of the Thredbo River, Lake Crackenback Resort & Spa offers studio apartments, chalets and lakeview apartments, all fully self-contained with kitchens and private balconies. Guests can unwind at the full-service day spa, indoor heated pool, gym, sauna and on-site restaurant. The resort sits a 15-minute drive from Thredbo and has private driveway access to Bullocks Flat Skitube terminal (0.5km), making it uniquely central to all three major ski fields.

stays.name: Banjo Paterson Inn
stays.short_description: Iconic Jindabyne pub-hotel with 40 rooms, two restaurants, three bars and Kosciuszko Brewhouse on site.
stays.long_description: A true Snowy Mountains institution, the Banjo Paterson Inn sits in the heart of Jindabyne with lakeside views and vibrant pub atmosphere. Rooms range from budget doubles to family loft suites, and guests have immediate access to Clancy's Brasserie, The Overflow burger-and-pizza bar, and the multi-award-winning Kosciuszko Brewhouse. Live music, nightly events and a continental breakfast (boxed, in-room) make this a lively choice for ski groups and families alike.

stays.name: Horizons Lake Jindabyne
stays.short_description: 4-star hotel formerly Rydges Horizons with 120 lake-view apartments, indoor pool, two restaurants and complimentary breakfast.
stays.long_description: Horizons Lake Jindabyne (previously known as Rydges Horizons Snowy Mountains) is Jindabyne's largest full-service hotel, offering 120 individually decorated apartments with full kitchens, washing machines and lake-facing balconies. The property features an indoor heated pool, outdoor tennis court, gym, ski equipment storage, two dining venues (including the premium Embers Fireside Restaurant) and two bars. Free breakfast is included in most room rates, making it great value for ski families.

stays.name: The Station (Snow Stay)
stays.short_description: Budget-friendly Perisher-owned motel and apartment resort 7km from Jindabyne town, with restaurant, bar and shuttle connections.
stays.long_description: The Station is run by Perisher Resort and sits 7km south of Jindabyne town centre on Snowy River Way. It offers no-frills motel rooms and self-contained one and two-bedroom apartments, ideal for budget ski groups. On-site facilities include a restaurant, bar, guest laundry and free parking. Reception is open until midnight (2am Fridays), and Epic Australia Pass holders receive 15% off motel rates.

stays.name: Kosciuszko Chalet Hotel
stays.short_description: Historic ski-in ski-out lodge at Charlotte Pass – Australia's highest resort – with all-inclusive winter packages including meals and lift passes.
stays.long_description: Situated at the heart of Charlotte Pass Village at around 1755m elevation, the Kosciuszko Chalet Hotel is Australia's most remote and highest alpine lodge, accessible only by oversnow transport from Perisher in winter. Winter packages include oversnow transfer, lift passes, daily breakfast and a three-course à la carte dinner, plus complimentary Kids Club running to 9pm. The historic property has a cosy lounge with open fireplace, live music and bar; room types range from classic rooms sleeping up to 6 to luxury suites.
stays.address: Kosciuszko Road, Charlotte Pass, Kosciuszko National Park NSW 2630

stays.name: Lake Jindabyne Hotel
stays.short_description: Lakefront pub-hotel with 40 rooms, popular bistro and sauna, rated #1 hotel in Jindabyne on Tripadvisor.
stays.long_description: Occupying a prime position on McLure Circuit at the water's edge, the Lake Jindabyne Hotel combines affordable motel-style rooms with a well-regarded bistro, sauna, indoor pool, games room and outdoor terrace with sweeping lake views. Rooms are modest but clean, and free breakfast is included. The bistro is famous locally for generous steaks and pub classics, and the outdoor lakeside terrace is a favourite apres-ski spot.

stays.name: Jindy Inn
stays.short_description: Rated #1 B&B/Inn in Jindabyne on Tripadvisor – 14-room boutique motel with lake views, fireside lounge and beauty therapy.
stays.long_description: The Jindy Inn sits on Clyde Street, a short stroll from Jindabyne town centre and within walking distance of cafes, bars and restaurants. All 14 rooms are ensuite and feature either a balcony with lake views or a terrace onto a rose garden. A cosy fireside lounge makes it popular in winter, and the property offers beauty therapy, waxing and facial services. A hot buffet breakfast is served daily, making it ideal for ski-day fuelling.

stays.name: Discovery Holiday Park – Jindabyne
stays.short_description: Lakefront caravan park and cabin resort with BBQ, laundry, bouncing pillow and lake access; 20 min to ski resorts.
stays.long_description: Perched on the shores of Lake Jindabyne, Discovery Parks offers powered and unpowered camping sites alongside modern self-contained cabins ranging from budget to deluxe two-bedroom with fireplace. The park is well-maintained with a kiosk, laundry, bike station, playground and tennis court. Cabins have full kitchens and the lakefront location means you can walk or cycle the foreshore path into town. Pets are allowed seasonally (summer).

stays.name: Aspen Chalets
stays.short_description: Self-contained chalet-style apartments in Jindabyne, popular with families seeking home-away-from-home ski accommodation.
stays.long_description: Aspen Chalets offers a collection of fully self-contained chalet and apartment-style properties in and around Jindabyne, each equipped with full kitchens, lounge areas and parking. Properties vary in size from studio to multi-bedroom configurations, catering to couples and large groups. The chalet aesthetic – with ski storage, mountain décor and proximity to town – makes them a perennial favourite for ski season.

stays.name: Snowy Mountains Resort & Function Centre
stays.short_description: 3-star country hotel in Adaminaby with log fireplace, restaurant, recreation room and proximity to Lake Eucumbene.
stays.long_description: Located in the heritage township of Adaminaby, 45km north of Jindabyne, the Snowy Mountains Resort & Function Centre is a family-run property popular for weddings, functions and ski-season stopovers. Rooms feature memory foam beds, flat-screen TVs and tea/coffee facilities, and the restaurant serves cooked-to-order breakfast. A log fireplace in the guest lounge, billiards table and arcade games round out the facilities. Note: this property is best suited as a base for Charlotte Pass or Selwyn Snowfields rather than Thredbo/Perisher.

stays.name: Kookaburra Lodge
stays.short_description: Best-value lodge in Jindabyne – renovated 12-room property with drying room, free breakfast and walking distance to town.
stays.long_description: Kookaburra Lodge on Clyde Street is consistently rated the best budget accommodation in the Snowy Mountains. The newly renovated property has 12 rooms ranging from motel-style ensuite doubles to dorm-style bunks, with all linen provided. A drying room is a major ski-season asset, and the communal recreation room has tea/coffee facilities, microwave, fridge, TV, lounge and fireplace. Continental breakfast is included, and the town centre is a short stroll away.

stays.name: Chalet Jindabyne
stays.short_description: Family-owned 13-room ski lodge on Gippsland Street with sauna, fireplace, billiards and continental breakfast included.
stays.long_description: Chalet Jindabyne is a local, family-run ski lodge occupying three storeys and 720sqm of mountain living space. Thirteen rooms (10 ensuite, 3 shared bathroom) spread across family and twin configurations, and guests enjoy a sauna, billiards table, large balcony with BBQ, and cosy open fire in the lounge. The continental breakfast is buffet-style, Netflix is available in the TV lounge, and the 2-minute drive to Lake Jindabyne and 30-minute drive to Thredbo or Perisher make it a reliable mid-range ski base.

stays.name: Panorama Jindabyne
stays.short_description: Motel with 25 rooms and sweeping Snowy Mountains and lake panoramas; seasonal restaurant/bar and ski storage on site.
stays.long_description: Panorama Jindabyne sits on Nettin Circuit with unobstructed views over Lake Jindabyne and the surrounding mountain ranges. The 25 air-conditioned rooms span budget to lake-view premium options, and a three-bedroom apartment is available in winter. Breakfast is included during winter. The on-site restaurant and bar operates seasonally, and ski storage is available. Off-street parking and wheelchair-accessible rooms are also offered.

stays.name: Siesta Villa Motel
stays.short_description: 31-room lakeside motel on Jerrara Drive with spa bath, on-site bistro and ski equipment rental, 3km from town centre.
stays.long_description: Siesta Villa is a 3-star motel located on Jerrara Drive with 31 rooms, all featuring balconies and lake views. The property includes a restaurant and bar (Lakeside Bistro & Bar), spa bath, on-site ski rental, and a games room with pool table. Under new management as of recent years, it represents good value for families and couples seeking a quieter lakeside setting away from the main strip.

stays.name: Carinya Village Jindabyne
stays.short_description: Secluded 15-room mountain lodge on 14km-from-slopes lake access with restaurant, conference rooms and traditional architecture.
stays.long_description: Carinya Village is a boutique mountain lodge set on Carinya Lane, offering 15 individually furnished rooms in a tranquil setting. The property includes a restaurant, conference facilities, ski gear storage, guest garden and picnic area. Check-in is from 4pm and limited to guests over 18, making it better suited to couples and corporate groups. Built in 1979, the traditional mountain architecture and garden setting provide a genuine alpine feel.

stays.name: Crackenback Farm Restaurant & Guesthouse
stays.short_description: Award-winning 6-room boutique guesthouse by Glenn Murcutt, 5 min from Jindabyne with acclaimed French country restaurant and ski valley views.
stays.long_description: Designed by Glenn Murcutt and set in the Crackenback Valley five minutes from Jindabyne, this intimate guesthouse has six beautifully appointed rooms, each with a queen bed and private bathroom, with cooked country breakfast included. The French country-farmhouse restaurant has a cathedral ceiling, an open fireplace, and a well-curated wine list – and draws accolades for some of the best food in the Snowy Mountains. Less than 10 minutes from Bullocks Flat Skitube terminal and 20 minutes from Thredbo Village.

stays.name: Alps Lakeview Lodge
stays.short_description: Budget lakeside lodge in East Jindabyne with self-catering rooms, free parking and lake proximity.
stays.long_description: Formerly known as East Lake Travellers Lodge, Alps Lakeview Lodge sits on Jerrara Drive in East Jindabyne within 500m of Lake Jindabyne. The property offers budget-friendly rooms with mini-fridges, microwaves and toaster ovens, making it popular with self-sufficient ski groups. Free WiFi, parking and laundry facilities are available, and the lake foreshore path provides direct access to the main town area without needing to drive.

stays.name: Snow Ski Apartments – Jindabyne
stays.short_description: Self-contained ski apartments in central Jindabyne, offering affordable self-catering accommodation for ski groups.
stays.long_description: Snow Ski Apartments Jindabyne provides a range of self-contained apartments in Jindabyne town, ideal for ski groups who prefer the flexibility of cooking their own meals. Properties typically feature fully equipped kitchens, separate living areas, laundry facilities and ski storage, with the town's supermarkets, restaurants and ski hire shops within walking distance. Booking is managed through the Jindabyne Ski Accommodation platform.

stays.name: Snowy Valley Jindabyne
stays.short_description: Budget shared-room accommodation in Jindabyne, popular with ski groups looking for the lowest-cost base option.
stays.long_description: Snowy Valley Jindabyne offers share-room dormitory-style accommodation for budget-conscious ski travellers. Rooms typically sleep 4–5 people and share bathroom facilities. The property is walking distance to the ski hire and supermarkets in town. Basic but functional for those whose priority is spending their money on the mountain rather than the accommodation.

stays.name: Alpine Country Holidays – Jindabyne Apartments
stays.short_description: Curated portfolio of handpicked self-contained apartments and chalets in Jindabyne and surrounds, bookable through a local boutique agency.
stays.long_description: Alpine Country Holidays is a boutique local accommodation manager offering a handpicked selection of modern apartments, cosy chalets and spacious country homes across Jindabyne, Lake Crackenback and Thredbo surrounds. Properties range from studio apartments to large group homes sleeping 10+, all with full kitchens, lounge areas and high-quality furnishings. Guests report excellent locations within walking distance of Jindabyne's restaurants and bars.

stays.name: Jindabyne & Snowy Mountains Accommodation Centre
stays.short_description: Local agency offering a wide range of self-contained Jindabyne units and homes, plus ski and snowboard rental packages.
stays.long_description: The Jindabyne and Snowy Mountains Accommodation Centre manages a large portfolio of self-contained holiday homes, units and apartments across Jindabyne. The agency's point of difference is bundled ski/snowboard rental packages, allowing groups to book accommodation and gear hire together at a discounted rate. Properties suit couples through to large family groups, and the booking service is available online with phone support.

stays.name: Jindabyne Ski Accommodation – Holiday Rentals
stays.short_description: Online rental platform offering 50+ self-contained ski apartments, townhouses and chalets across Jindabyne and the Snowy Mountains.
stays.long_description: Jindabyne Ski Accommodation is the Snowy Mountains' leading online holiday rental platform, listing over 50 self-contained properties ranging from affordable studio apartments to award-winning luxury chalets. All properties are fully equipped with kitchens and most include ski storage. The platform's high occupancy rates and regular repeat guests reflect consistent quality. Properties are spread across Jindabyne town, Crackenback and Thredbo approaches.

stays.name: Snowy Mountains Airbnb / Holiday Rentals (Jindabyne)
stays.short_description: Wide range of private Airbnb homes and holiday rentals in Jindabyne, from lakefront studios to large group homes with ski storage.
stays.long_description: Jindabyne has a large inventory of privately listed Airbnb and VRBO properties, particularly popular during the July–August ski season when they often represent the best value for groups of 4–10. Options range from lakefront studios to 5-bedroom homes with hot tubs and mountain views. Booking well in advance (3+ months) is essential for peak dates. Many listings include ski storage, drying rooms and are within 5 minutes' drive of Thredbo or Perisher roads.

stays.name: Jindabyne Ski Lodge Accommodation Centre – Private Lodges
stays.short_description: Network of private ski club lodges in Jindabyne available for casual bookings, with drying rooms and communal ski-season facilities.
stays.long_description: Beyond the commercially listed hotels, Jindabyne has a thriving network of private ski club lodges that open casual bookings in peak season. These typically offer bunk or twin rooms in a communal lodge setting with drying rooms, full kitchens, fireplaces and buffet dinners. They cater primarily to ski groups seeking an authentic lodge atmosphere at prices below commercial hotels. Booking is usually via direct contact with individual clubs or through snowaccommodation.com.au.

stays.name: Kosciuszko Brewing Accommodation (Banjo Paterson Complex)
stays.short_description: Self-contained apartment-style rooms in the Banjo Paterson Inn complex, with access to on-site brewery, restaurants and bars.
stays.long_description: The Banjo Paterson Inn complex on Kosciuszko Road includes apartment-style accommodation with loft configurations, lake views and direct access to the Kosciuszko Brewhouse, Clancy's Brasserie and The Overflow. These are among the most social rooms in Jindabyne, favoured by groups who want to walk from bed to bar to slopes without needing a car. Quad loft rooms comfortably sleep 4–6 and include balconies and lake views. The vibrant pub atmosphere means this isn't the quietest option.

stays.name: Snowgate Motel & Apartments
stays.short_description: Affordable family motel with on-site restaurant, bar, sauna, and ski hire in the heart of Berridale.
stays.long_description: The Snowgate Motel is a family-run property offering bunk and family rooms designed for ski groups, plus self-contained apartments for longer stays. On-site facilities include the SnowGate Restaurant (breakfast and dinner, international menu), a bar, hot tub, and sauna - rare amenities in Berridale at this price point. Ski equipment hire is available on site, making it a practical one-stop shop for budget mountain trips.
stays.address: Lot 3 Southern Cross Drive, Berridale NSW 2628

stays.name: Cottonwood Lodge
stays.short_description: Locally owned ski lodge with drying room, fireplace lounge, bar, and rooms for couples to large groups.
stays.long_description: Cottonwood Lodge is a long-established, locally owned ski lodge purpose-built for winter accommodation. It offers a range of room types from double rooms to family rooms sleeping up to 8, all with private bathrooms, flat-screen TVs, and heating. Communal facilities include a dining room with open fireplace, a licensed bar, BBQ area, games room with pool table, drying room for wet ski gear, and a seasonal outdoor pool. One of the few Berridale properties with a confirmed drying room.

stays.name: Snowy Mountains Motor Inn
stays.short_description: Large 41-room motel on Jindabyne Road specialising in group and school bookings with buffet breakfast included.
stays.long_description: The Snowy Mountains Motor Inn is one of the larger properties in Berridale, with 41 rooms and capacity for up to 220 guests across its group-booking packages. The property primarily caters to school camps and sporting groups but accepts general public bookings. Rooms feature flat-screen TVs, kettles, and refrigerators; buffet breakfast is served each morning. Positioned on Jindabyne Road making it convenient for the Perisher and Thredbo runs.

stays.name: Southern Cross Motor Inn & Tourist Park
stays.short_description: Large budget motel on six acres with restaurant, bar, fireplace lounge, ski hire shop, and 63 rooms.
stays.long_description: The Southern Cross Motor Inn is the biggest single accommodation complex in Berridale, set on six acres with a 63-room motel plus caravan/tourist park. An on-site 100-seat restaurant, bar/lounge with open fire, ski hire shop, and lift ticket organising service make it a self-contained ski base. Rooms include standard and deluxe options, most with kitchenette, fridge, and flat-screen TV. Value ratings are consistently high in reviews despite the basic styling.

stays.name: Berridale Inn Hotel Motel
stays.short_description: Classic country pub hotel with 7 en-suite rooms, public bar, lounge bar, restaurant, and a kids playroom.
stays.long_description: The Berridale Inn is the town's main pub and only hotel-motel in a traditional Australian pub format. The 7 en-suite rooms sleep up to 7 each and have coffee-making facilities, TV, and heating. The adjoining restaurant and bar are open seven days, and the premises include a public bar with TAB and Keno, a family-friendly lounge bar with pool table, a beer garden, and a kids' playroom. Note: the pub has experienced temporary closures; verify current trading before booking.

stays.name: Snowdream Motel
stays.short_description: Owner-operated budget motel in central Berridale with 40 rooms, communal kitchen, fireplace lounge, and help-yourself continental breakfast.
stays.long_description: The Snowdream Motel is a consistently well-reviewed budget option in central Berridale. The 40 rooms range from singles to family rooms sleeping up to 8, most with queen bed, bunks, and en suite. Communal facilities include a large kitchen, dining area, lounge with fireplace, and BBQ area. Help-yourself continental breakfast is included. The motel's value rating is one of the highest in Berridale at 4.5/5 on Tripadvisor.

stays.name: Sierra Villa Lodge
stays.short_description: Bed-and-breakfast lodge in a quiet Berridale street offering relaxed, homely accommodation for families and groups.
stays.long_description: Sierra Villa Lodge is a B&B-style lodge property on Oliver Street offering affordable ski-season accommodation in a quiet, residential setting. The property aims for a relaxed, homely atmosphere with a communal lounge area. Amenities include TV, games room with pool table, and BBQ area. Reviews note the friendly host environment and good value for families. A separate self-contained 2-bedroom unit also available.

stays.name: Berridale Alpine Retreat
stays.short_description: Spacious self-contained cabin in Berridale township, walking distance to cafes, sleeping 6-8 guests.
stays.long_description: A guest-favourite Airbnb cabin in central Berridale, within walking distance to the pub, cafe, restaurant, and winery. The cabin sleeps up to 8 guests (6 comfortably) and is positioned as a practical ski base - Jindabyne is 15 minutes away and ski resorts are 45 minutes drive. Check-in during the June–September ski season is 4:30pm Mon–Thu; contact host for earlier times. Also listed on Stayz.

stays.name: Martini: Vintage Ski Lodge
stays.short_description: Heritage Snowy Scheme house decked out in 1960s ski nostalgia - records, martinis, and après-ski character.
stays.long_description: A top-rated Airbnb in Berridale that leans hard into vintage Australian ski culture. The property is a heritage Snowy Mountains Scheme-era house kitted out with 1960s decor, jazz and pop records, retro appliances, and the promise of après-ski martinis. Unique and characterful - this is the antidote to sterile motel rooms. Great for couples or groups wanting something memorable over budget-anonymous accommodation. Exact room count not disclosed by host.

stays.name: Rust on Kiparra
stays.short_description: Top-rated 3-bedroom artistic home with rustic recycled features, firepit, and 5-minute walk to the winery and pub.
stays.long_description: A top-guest-favourite Airbnb on Kiparra Street in Berridale, this 3-bedroom/2-bathroom home is custom-designed using recycled and handmade rustic materials. The open-plan layout includes full laundry, outdoor BBQ, firepit, and outdoor dining table. Linen and towels supplied, free WiFi included. Centrally located - 5-minute walk to the winery, pub, cafes, and shops. Drive times: Jindabyne 25 min, Thredbo/Perisher 50–55 min.

stays.name: Bliss Cabin @ Belaxed Farm
stays.short_description: Pet-friendly 1-bedroom farm cabin on 62.5 acres with firepit, mountain views, wildlife, and self-contained kitchen.
stays.long_description: A superhost Airbnb/Booking.com property set on a 62.5-acre farm outside Berridale at 360 Bobundara Road. The one-bedroom, 36 m² cabin has a kitchenette with oven and microwave, private bathroom, air-conditioning, patio with mountain views, outdoor fireplace, and sun terrace. Pet-friendly with a damage deposit. The property hosts kangaroos, wombats, and farm animals. Located 24 km from the snowfields and 29 km from Lake Jindabyne.

stays.name: Lappi Farm Cabins
stays.short_description: Pet-friendly Finnish-style cedar log cabins on the Snowy River with wood-fired sauna, campfire, and farmstay atmosphere.
stays.long_description: Lappi Farm is a Finnish-heritage farmstay offering five handcrafted solid cedar log cabins (built in the 1980s) on the banks of the Snowy River near Berridale. Each cabin is positioned for privacy with uninterrupted views of the river and Monaro Plains. Facilities include a traditional wood-fired Finnish sauna, campfire areas, and the opportunity to meet farm animals and spot platypus and wombats. Pet-friendly. Accessible by AWD only for some sections. Also listed on Airbnb as 'Mokki'. 2 hours from Canberra.

stays.name: Cooma Motor Inn
stays.short_description: Largest motel in Cooma CBD; 43 rooms ranging from standard queens to self-contained apartments.
stays.long_description: Cooma Motor Inn (formerly Sovereign Inn) sits centrally on Sharp Street with 43 well-appointed rooms including standard queen, twin, family, and self-contained one- and two-bedroom garden apartments. The property is next door to Rhythm Snowsports ski-hire and walking distance from the main café strip. A reliable base for ski season families who want kitchen facilities without the price premium of mountain resorts.

stays.name: Snow Season Motor Inn
stays.short_description: Largest-capacity motel in Cooma with 60 rooms; first motel on entry from Canberra/Sydney.
stays.long_description: Snow Season Motor Inn (formerly Marlborough Motor Inn) on the Monaro Highway is Cooma's biggest single motel, with 60 units spread across 4 low-rise buildings. The log-fire lobby bar and pool table give it a ski-lodge feel. Note: the on-site restaurant (Stockman's) is currently closed, but the bar remains open. Good choice for groups and coach tours given its scale and ample parking.

stays.name: Kinross Inn
stays.short_description: Well-appointed motel with indoor heated pool; short walk from CBD restaurants.
stays.long_description: Kinross Inn on Sharp Street offers a step up from the typical Cooma motel with an indoor heated saltwater pool, executive spa rooms, and family suites with kitchenettes. The property is set back from the highway for quiet, yet is less than a kilometre from the main café strip. A popular choice for ski families who want more than a basic room without paying mountain resort prices.

stays.name: White Manor Motel
stays.short_description: Highly-rated family-run motel 1.1 km from CBD; 12 immaculate rooms with mountain views.
stays.long_description: White Manor Motel consistently earns top TripAdvisor scores for cleanliness and is one of the best mid-range options in Cooma. The 12 air-conditioned rooms (queen, twin, family) feature smart TVs with Netflix, microwave, toaster, and fridge. The property sits on Sharp Street with mountain backdrop views. Small and personal - the antithesis of the highway chain motel.

stays.name: Nebula Motel
stays.short_description: Central boutique motel on Bombala Street; walking distance to shops and restaurants.
stays.long_description: Nestled in central Cooma, the Nebula Motel pitches itself as a boutique stay within walking distance of all town amenities - shops, restaurants, pubs, and the Visitors Centre. Popular with skiers who want to be on foot for the evening without needing a car. The motel has a solid review base (249 TripAdvisor reviews) and consistent scores for location and value.

stays.name: Altair Motel
stays.short_description: Boutique-style motel on Sharp Street designed as a home-away-from-home.
stays.long_description: The Altair Motel is a purpose-designed boutique motel on Sharp Street aiming for a homely atmosphere - a notch above the standard highway motel. Positive TripAdvisor scores (3.8 from 75 reviews) reflect comfortable rooms and friendly service. Centrally located near cafes and snowsports hire shops. Contact is primarily mobile-first.

stays.name: High Country Motel
stays.short_description: Quiet 40-unit motel with outdoor pool, bar, and restaurant; great for groups and coach tours.
stays.long_description: The High Country Motel on Chapman Street offers 40 rooms set in a quiet bush-adjacent location, away from highway noise. Amenities include an outdoor pool (summer only), bar with open fire, licensed restaurant, karaoke, and BBQ area. Well-suited to larger groups and coach tours. Renovated rooms include microwaves and bar fridges. Accepts credit cards.

stays.name: Cooma Motor Lodge
stays.short_description: 44-room Golden Chain motel next to Rhythm Snowsports hire; EV chargers on-site.
stays.long_description: The Cooma Motor Lodge (6 Sharp Street, Golden Chain member) has been a Cooma institution since 1965 and was renovated in 2007. With 44 rooms on two floors and EV chargers recently installed, it suits road-trippers and snowfield-bound drivers alike. It sits directly next to Rhythm Snowsports ski hire, making it exceptionally practical for ski season. The in-house bistro and log fire bar create an après-ski atmosphere.

stays.name: Alpine Hotel
stays.short_description: Central pub hotel with 27 rooms, bistro, and 10 beers on tap; TripAdvisor #1 best-value.
stays.long_description: The Alpine Hotel on Sharp Street is a renovated two-storey pub hotel with 27 guestrooms, an open fire lounge, and a bistro serving lunch and dinner 7 days. With 10 beers on tap and secure garage parking for motorcycles, it caters to a wide mix of travellers. Ranked #1 Best Value in Cooma on TripAdvisor. Pet policy: no pets. Airport shuttle: not available.

stays.name: Royal Hotel Cooma
stays.short_description: NSW State Heritage-listed sandstone pub (1858) with budget pub rooms and a popular bistro.
stays.long_description: The Royal Hotel is a heritage-listed two-storey dressed-freestone pub on the corner of Sharp and Lambie Streets, built in 1858 and listed on the NSW State Heritage Register in 1999. Pub-style rooms (shared bathrooms) are budget-priced - great for skiers on a tight budget. The Royal Bistro serves traditional Australian pub meals Tuesday–Sunday. The building's Georgian/Victorian character makes it one of Cooma's most photographed landmarks.
stays.address: 59-61 Lambie Street (cnr Sharp & Lambie), Cooma NSW 2630

stays.name: Cooma Hotel
stays.short_description: Oldest continuously operating hotel in Cooma (1862); bar, bistro, drive-through bottle shop.
stays.long_description: Built in 1862, the Cooma Hotel on the corner of Massie and Vale Streets claims the title of Cooma's oldest continually operating hotel. Beyond accommodation, it functions as a community hub with bar, bistro serving lunch and dinner, drive-through bottle shop, cinema, and function facilities. Budget pub-style rooms are available. Phone updated to +61 2 6404 7530 under new management.

stays.name: Ellstanmor Country Guesthouse
stays.short_description: Victorian-era B&B (1875) in Cooma CBD with 4 en-suite rooms; TripAdvisor #1 B&B.
stays.long_description: Ellstanmor Country Guesthouse occupies an 1875 Victorian home on Massie Street in the heart of Cooma's CBD. The property features ornate staircases, French doors, a library, parlour, and 4 queen rooms each with en-suite. Guests are served self-service continental or cooked-to-order country breakfasts. A treadmill, astronomical telescope, and genuine character distinguish this B&B from any motel. Rated #1 B&B in Cooma and in the top 10% of TripAdvisor properties globally.

stays.name: Nest Stays by Birdsnest
stays.short_description: Two boutique heritage terraces on Lambie Street by fashion brand birdsnest; luxury self-contained.
stays.long_description: Nest Stays comprises two lovingly restored 1860s heritage terrace homes on picturesque Lambie Street, curated by Australian fashion retailer birdsnest. Terrace 1 sleeps 6 adults across 3 bedrooms; Terrace 2 sleeps 6 across 4 bedrooms with an oversized stone bath. Both feature fully equipped kitchens, cosy lounges, underfloor hydronic heating, 100% linen bedding, iKou organic bath products, and private backyard patios with outdoor kitchens. TripAdvisor's top-rated property in Cooma (5.0/5, 24 reviews). Perfect for girlfriend groups or ski families wanting a premium basecamp.

stays.name: Cooma Holiday Park
stays.short_description: Family-friendly caravan park in central Cooma with cabins, powered and unpowered sites.
stays.long_description: Formerly the Cooma Snowy Mountains Tourist Park and now operating as Cooma Holiday Park, this central park at 286 Sharp Street sits on the Snowy Mountains Highway. Options range from self-contained Banksia Cabins (2 bedrooms, full kitchen, sleeps 4) to budget Snowgum Cabins and powered/unpowered caravan sites from $35/night. Facilities include mini golf, playground, activity room, and BBQ areas. Walking distance to town centre shops and cafes. The budget option for families and van travellers.
stays.address: 286 Sharp Street (Snowy Mountains Hwy), Cooma NSW 2630

stays.name: Alpine Country Motel
stays.short_description: Roadside motel on Snowy Mountains Hwy 5 km south of Cooma CBD; adjacent Metro Roadhouse café.
stays.long_description: The Alpine Country Motel (formerly Alpine Country Motor Inn) sits at 651 Snowy Mountains Highway on the approach from Jindabyne, 4–5 minutes south of central Cooma. On 4 acres of land with a Metro Roadhouse café attached, it's the first stop heading toward the ski fields from Cooma. Complimentary coffee for guests. The cheapest bookable rates in the Cooma area, often from $117/night.
stays.address: 651 Snowy Mountains Highway, Pine Valley, Cooma NSW 2630

stays.name: Cromwell House
stays.short_description: Boutique B&B; highly-rated heritage-style guesthouse near Cooma CBD (TripAdvisor 4.9/5).
stays.long_description: Cromwell House is a boutique guesthouse property in central Cooma with exceptional TripAdvisor scores (4.9/5 from 49 reviews), indicating a genuinely outstanding guest experience. The property includes breakfast and is listed in the TripAdvisor B&B/inn category. It represents Cooma's premium heritage accommodation tier alongside Ellstanmor and Nest Stays.

stays.name: Bunkhouse Motel
stays.short_description: Budget 29-unit motel centrally located 1 block from the RSL club; some self-contained units.
stays.long_description: The Bunkhouse Motel on Soho Street is a budget-friendly option with 29 units - 18 standard rooms and 11 self-contained units with cooking facilities. Ground-floor access, central heating, TV, and babysitting availability make it popular with budget ski families. One block from the Cooma Ex-Services Club (RSL) and central to the main street strip.

stays.name: Alkira Motel
stays.short_description: Well-reviewed motel near the Snowy Hydro Discovery Centre; family-friendly, TripAdvisor 4.1.
stays.long_description: The Alkira Motel earns strong TripAdvisor marks (4.1/5, 71 reviews) and appears repeatedly in best-value and family-friendly shortlists for Cooma. Located close to the Snowy Hydro Discovery Centre and within reach of the town's cafes and snowsports hire shops. A solid mid-tier option for those prioritising cleanliness and value.

stays.name: Yorozuya
stays.short_description: Historic prestige ryokan with a nationally registered cultural property bathhouse (Momoyama-buro) and abundant natural hot spring flow.
stays.long_description: Yorozuya is one of Yudanaka's most storied inns, blending Meiji-era elegance with modern comforts. Its showpiece is the Momoyama-buro (桃山風呂), a stunning wooden bathhouse registered as a Tangible Cultural Property of Japan, featuring soaring ceilings and ornate joinery. The property offers both indoor and outdoor rotenburo, kaiseki cuisine using north-Nagano mountain and river produce, and - since 2023 - a private spa suite called 'Bon'. Shuttle service available to Yudanaka Station and Snow Monkey Park.
stays.notes: Momoyama-buro is a registered Tangible Cultural Property of Japan. Private SPA 'Bon' opened Feb 2023 - 2 sauna types + private bath. Highly recommended for special occasions.

stays.name: Hotel Issa-tei / Issa no Komichi Biyu no Yado
stays.name_local: 一茶のこみち 美湯の宿
stays.short_description: Mid-sized onsen ryokan with 100% natural flowing hot springs including a rooftop outdoor bath and renowned hot spring management by an in-house 'onsen meister'.
stays.long_description: Named after the famous haiku poet Kobayashi Issa who was born in nearby Kashiwabara, this ryokan sits in central Yudanaka and manages three hot spring sources producing soft alkaline water (弱アルカリ性単純泉) prized for skin-beautifying properties. All baths are 100% kakenagashi (continuously flowing, never recycled). Rooms range from classic Japanese tatami to Japanese-Western hybrid and premium suites with private outdoor baths. The property offers a free shuttle to Yudanaka Station, Snow Monkey Park, and Shiga Kogen ski areas, with an English hotline operated by an English-speaking coordinator.
stays.notes: English hotline: 080-6938-3361 (Craig Shaw). Day-trip bathing available ¥800. Private reserved bath ¥3,000 for 2 places. Free shuttle to Shiga Kogen ski areas is a major benefit for skiers. Tattoo policy: private baths available - public bath policy not explicitly confirmed as tattoo-friendly.

stays.name: Kambayashi Hotel Senjukaku
stays.short_description: Closest ryokan to Snow Monkey Park, with Nagano Prefecture's largest hot spring source and luxurious kaiseki dining.
stays.long_description: Senjukaku sits at the end of the road near the Snow Monkey Park trailhead in Kambayashi Onsen, a quieter sister village to Yudanaka. The hotel boasts the largest natural hot spring source in Nagano Prefecture - 720 litres per minute, constantly drained for freshness - with communal indoor and outdoor baths, and private hinoki cypress or granite kashikiri baths (¥1,500/45 min). The traditional Japanese garden with 100-year-old sakura trees, koi stream, and lobby art exhibitions lend an atmosphere of cultivated elegance. Kaiseki meals use Shinshu beef, golden gamefowl, and seasonal local vegetables. Catering to international guests including for vegetarian and gluten-free dietary needs.
stays.address: 1410 Hirao, Kambayashi Onsen, Yamanouchi, Shimotakai-gun, Nagano 381-0401
stays.notes: Note from Expedia: 'some properties do not permit guests with tattoos to use the onsite public bathing facilities' - public baths likely not_allowed for tattooed guests; private baths available. Can cater to vegetarian, gluten-free, dietary restrictions if requested at reservation. Indoor heated pool free (bring swimsuit). The largest natural hot spring source in Nagano Prefecture.

stays.name: Shimaya Ryokan
stays.short_description: Traditional family-run ryokan with flowing hinoki cypress hot spring bath, communal bath, and private rental bath.
stays.long_description: Shimaya (島屋) is a quietly elegant, old-style ryokan that has maintained traditional hospitality for generations in the heart of Yudanaka. The property features three bathing options: the hinoki (Japanese cypress) bath called 'Hagi no Yu' (萩の湯), the communal large bath 'Shiga no Yu' (志賀の湯), and a private rental bath. All hot springs are 100% natural source water. The proprietor Mr. Yumoto is known for fast communication in English by email. Unlike most ryokan, food is offered as an add-on (not automatically included), making it a more flexible and affordable option. Meals are Japanese home-style cooking using seasonal local ingredients.
stays.notes: Meal plan is flexible - breakfast ¥800-1,300, dinner ¥2,500-4,500 as add-ons. Good-value choice. Shimaya Soba restaurant is a separate establishment (see eats). Owner responds to English emails. Price range may vary - ¥24,000-29,000/room based on TripAdvisor data.

stays.name: Tawaraya Ryokan
stays.short_description: Charming small ryokan with reservable private outdoor onsen garden bath, English-speaking staff, and excellent kaiseki meals.
stays.long_description: Tawaraya Ryokan is a 10-room traditional inn set around a tranquil garden in central Yudanaka, a 5-minute walk from the station. The outdoor garden rotenburo can be reserved privately (30-minute slots) and has drawn consistent praise from international guests as one of the most atmospheric baths in the area. Staff are well-regarded for their English ability and warm service. Rooms feature tatami mats, futon bedding, and shoji screens. Kaiseki multi-course dinners featuring seasonal local produce and Shinshu beef, with a Japanese set breakfast. Souvenir shop on site.
stays.notes: Highly rated for English service and private garden onsen. 'Amazing kaiseki meals worth ordering in advance.' - Guest review. Rooms have private toilet but shared bathrooms (shared with Japanese facilities).

stays.name: Aburaya Tousen
stays.short_description: Upscale modern ryokan with private room onsen, rooftop rotenburo, and in-house boutique and gift shop.
stays.long_description: Aburaya Tousen is a stylish mid-luxury ryokan blending traditional aesthetics with contemporary design touches. Located about an 8-minute walk from Yudanaka Station, it is particularly popular with couples and international guests. Rooms include suites with private open-air onsen baths on balconies, and the communal baths include an outdoor rooftop rotenburo with panoramic views and a jacuzzi. The on-site restaurant serves kaiseki cuisine for dinner in private dining rooms. An on-site boutique carries premium regional crafts and chopsticks. Staff are noted for being thoughtful and welcoming to international guests.
stays.notes: #8 of 81 onsen ryokan in Yamanouchi on TripAdvisor. Owner greeted guests personally. Known for excellent chopsticks in gift shop. Some staff speak English. Rooftop rotenburo particularly praised.

stays.name: Uotoshi Ryokan
stays.short_description: Small traditional ryokan with gender-separated communal onsen and rooms overlooking the valley, 500m from Yudanaka Station.
stays.long_description: Uotoshi Ryokan (魚敏) is a compact 8-room inn offering an authentic low-key ryokan experience in Yudanaka. The communal onsen is separated by gender and is open 24 hours, with the traditional mineral water providing a pleasantly aromatic and perfectly tempered soak. Rooms are spacious Japanese-style with excellent mountain and valley views; balcony rooms facing the fountain are particularly recommended by guests. The half-board rate is standard and meals must be confirmed before check-in. Located just 500 metres from Yudanaka Station.
stays.notes: Rated $71-99 USD per room (TripAdvisor). Half-board guests must check in by 6pm for dinner. 24-hour public bath. Highly affordable by Yudanaka standards. TripAdvisor rating 4.3/5 from 36 reviews.

stays.name: Honke Bansho
stays.short_description: Traditional Yudanaka ryokan with onsen and local Shinshu cuisine in central hot spring town.
stays.long_description: Honke Bansho (本家伴勝) is a long-standing traditional ryokan in the Yudanaka Onsen district. As a 'honke' (main house) property, it emphasises traditional hospitality rooted in Nagano inn-keeping heritage. The property offers communal hot spring bathing and seasonal kaiseki-style meals featuring Shinshu regional specialities including river fish from the Chikuma River, wild mountain vegetables (sansai), and local mushrooms. The intimate atmosphere suits travellers seeking an authentic Japanese inn experience away from larger hotel crowds.
stays.notes: Note: Do not confuse with 'Honke Bankyu' (本家伴久) which is a separate, unrelated luxury ryokan in Yunishigawa Onsen, Nikko (Tochigi Prefecture). Honke Bansho is specific to Yudanaka. Limited online booking availability - best booked via Jalan or Rakuten Travel. English spoken is limited to no.

stays.name: Hotel Sanyokan
stays.short_description: Mid-range hotel with large communal onsen complex - one of the biggest in Yudanaka - near the station.
stays.long_description: Hotel Sanyokan (山陽館) is a large-format traditional hotel in Yudanaka Onsen with one of the most extensive onsen bath complexes in the town, featuring multiple pools including a tea bath, waterfall massage pool, sauna, and steam room. The sprawling layout and multiple bath types attract both ryokan guests and day-trippers. Rooms range from spacious tatami-style (some with mini-kitchenettes) to private Western rooms. The hotel has a communal lounge area with TV and tatami seating. A casual in-house kitchen/diner operates during meal hours. Located close to Yudanaka Station.
stays.notes: Note: 'Hotel Yudanaka' as listed on some OTA sites may refer to this property or an adjacent hotel - both are similar large-format budget onsen hotels near the station. The property has also served as a community bathhouse for locals. Free shuttle to Snow Monkey Park. Rated as one of the largest onsen complexes in Yudanaka town.

stays.name: Yudanaka Onsen Yamazakiya
stays.name_local: 湯田中温泉 山崎屋
stays.short_description: Intimate family-run ryokan with private onsen access, genuine hospitality from host Akira and family, and complimentary transport to Snow Monkey Park.
stays.long_description: Yamazakiya is a small family-operated ryokan run by Akira and his family (mother Kiyoko is a beloved local figure) on the charming main street of Yudanaka. Unlike most ryokan in the area, all onsen baths are private-use only, meaning guests need never share the bath - a significant advantage for tattooed travellers or those seeking complete privacy. Akira also holds keys to two public onsen nearby for guests who want that option. Traditional kaiseki breakfast and dinner are exceptional, featuring ultra-fresh local produce. Complimentary car service to the station and Snow Monkey Park trailhead. Rooms are tatami with kotatsu (heated table), futon, and river view options.
stays.notes: Tattoo policy: ALLOWED in private baths - all baths are private-use only so tattoos are not an issue. Host Akira also has access to public onsen for guests who wish. Rated 9.x on Booking.com. Exceptional guest-host warmth. Yukata worn correctly taught by staff. Complimentary Shinshu apple given to guests. Highly recommended for first-time ryokan visitors.

stays.name: Yudanaka Ryokan Hakura
stays.short_description: Well-regarded mid-range ryokan with private-use onsen booking system, multilingual staff, and dietary-accommodating kaiseki meals.
stays.long_description: Ryokan Hakura is a 5-minute walk from Yudanaka Station and offers both Japanese tatami rooms and Western-style rooms. The house onsen (100% kakenagashi natural hot spring) can be booked privately by room in 50-minute slots, ensuring guests never have to share. Staff are multilingual (English and Japanese). Unusually for a rural Nagano ryokan, the kitchen caters to various dietary needs including vegetarian, Muslim, and allergy-specific requirements with advance notice. Seasonal kaiseki meals feature Shinshu beef and locally foraged ingredients. Breakfast included; dinner add-on recommended.
stays.notes: Onsen available: 15:00-19:00 (shared access), 19:00-next day 9:00 (private booking by room, 50-min slots). Accommodates vegetarian, Muslim, allergy diets - request 24 hours in advance. Host owner is very helpful with transport arrangements. Also listed on Expedia under 'Ryokan near Shiga Kogen Ski Area'.

stays.name: Hotel Tsubakino
stays.short_description: Mid-range hotel with rooftop outdoor onsen on the 5th floor, nightly wine bar, and excellent Japanese breakfasts, about 10 minutes walk from the station.
stays.long_description: Hotel Tsubakino is a relaxed and comfortable onsen hotel set in the hills above Yudanaka, offering both Japanese-style tatami rooms and Western rooms. The signature feature is the 5th-floor open-air rotenburo with panoramic mountain views - especially spectacular in winter snow. Private outdoor baths are available in select premium rooms. The hotel also features a charming nightly wine bar (an unexpected find in rural Nagano) and serves highly regarded Japanese breakfasts. Staff are described as attentive and helpful. A 'monkey bus' for day trips to Snow Monkey Park departs from the property.
stays.notes: Private outdoor rooftop onsen (5F) for couples available at additional cost. Nightly wine bar is a popular après-onsen hangout. Monkey bus departs daily. The private outdoor bath for a parent/child duo is highly reviewed.

stays.name: Hotarutei Villas
stays.short_description: Exclusive 2-villa property next to Snow Monkey Park with private indoor-outdoor natural hot spring baths, full seasonal dining, and luxury self-contained villas.
stays.long_description: Hotarutei Villas are a pair of high-end self-contained villas built in 2017 adjacent to the historic Hotarutei restaurant (est. 1987) in Kanbayashi, an 8-minute walk from the Snow Monkey Park trail entrance. Each villa sleeps 2-4 and features a private natural hot spring bath (half indoor, half outdoor), two bedrooms, spacious living room, kitchenette, and balcony. Fridge comes stocked with complimentary water, Shinshu apple juice, fresh milk, gelato, and Yebisu beer. Seasonal course dining available at the attached restaurant. The villas are constructed from a historic farmhouse relocated from Niigata. The 7-Eleven on Route 292 is a 5-minute drive.
stays.notes: Only 2 villas - books out fast in ski season and Snow Monkey peak season (Jan-Mar). Tattoo policy: ALLOWED - private baths only, no public bath on site. Price range: ¥22,000-74,000 per night (Snow Monkey Resorts listing). Nearest convenience store: 7-Eleven on R292 (5 min drive) or Lawson at Yudanaka Station (7 min drive / 50 min walk).

stays.name: Aibiya
stays.short_description: International-friendly upscale hostel in central Yudanaka, run by a welcoming Japanese-Korean couple, with dorm beds and private rooms.
stays.long_description: Aibiya is the primary budget accommodation option in Yudanaka, combining hostel practicality with ryokan-style warmth. The hosts are a Japanese-Korean couple who speak English fluently and provide personalised recommendations for the area. Accommodation ranges from 4-bed dormitories to private rooms in both tatami and Western styles. A daily breakfast combining Japanese and Western dishes is served. While Aibiya does not have its own onsen, the hosts can direct guests to nearby public hot spring baths. The guesthouse attracts a largely international crowd and is the social hub of the Yudanaka backpacker scene.
stays.notes: Check-in cut-off 20:00 - contact property if arriving late. No onsen on-site; hosts direct guests to nearby public baths (access to public onsen in Yudanaka area is easy). Tattoo: ALLOWED - no public onsen on-site so no restrictions. Excellent English spoken. Rated 10/10 on Expedia for service.

stays.name: Yudanaka Brewery Complex U (Inn)
stays.name_local: ゆダナカ ブルワリーコンプレックスU (宿泊)
stays.short_description: Modern craft-brewery-anchored complex with accommodation, day-trip onsen on the 2nd floor, and on-site Shinshu food and beer.
stays.long_description: The Yudanaka Brewery Complex U is a contemporary multi-purpose tourist complex opened in 2022 that combines a craft brewery, restaurant, and day-trip onsen baths under one roof. While primarily a day-trip destination (see also in the Eats section for the restaurant), the complex also offers accommodation in modern rooms. The 2nd-floor day-trip onsen is open 10:00-18:00. On-site craft beers are brewed using water from Yudanaka Onsen spring water. The complex is a 5-minute drive from Yudanaka Station in the Sano area, with 30 parking spaces.
stays.notes: Primarily a day-trip complex. Day-trip onsen and restaurant open 10:00-18:00. Food LO: 17:00. Parking: 30 spaces free. QR-code ordering in English available. Accommodation confirmation needs direct contact with property. Also listed in eats as 'yudanaka-brewery-complex-u'.

stays.name: Snow Monkey Resorts (Yamanouchi Area Booking Hub)
stays.name_local: スノーモンキーリゾーツ
stays.short_description: English-language concierge and booking service for Yamanouchi-area accommodation, including exclusive properties with full English support.
stays.long_description: Snow Monkey Resorts is an English-language booking and concierge service specialising in the Yamanouchi region - Yudanaka, Snow Monkey Park, and Shiga Kogen. Rather than a single property, they represent multiple partner hotels and ryokan in the area, providing full English support for international travellers. Properties include Hotel Grand Phenix (Shiga Kogen), Hotel Sunny Shiga, T Hotel Ryuoo, and others. They also provide ski passes, transfers, and local activity booking. For travellers uncomfortable with Japanese-only booking systems, Snow Monkey Resorts provides a critical bridge.
stays.address: Yamanouchi, Shimotakai-gun, Nagano (booking service - various properties)
stays.notes: This entry represents the Snow Monkey Resorts booking hub. Individual properties include Hotel Grand Phenix Okushiga, Hotel Sunny Shiga, T Hotel Ryuoo (Ryuoo Ski Park area). All properties booked via SMR include English concierge. Highly recommended for first-time visitors to the area. Partner property Kambayashi Hotel Senjukaku is also listed as a separate entry.

stays.name: Wafu no Yado Masuya
stays.short_description: Traditional Japanese-style inn with communal hot spring bathing, accepting cards (no cash required), near Yudanaka Station.
stays.long_description: Masuya is a traditional ryokan in the Yudanaka Onsen area offering classic Japanese hospitality with a communal hot spring bath. The property is notable for explicitly accepting credit cards (unlike many rural Nagano establishments) and for its cashless payment capability - a practical advantage for international travellers. Guests must contact the property in advance to reserve public bathing access, and the property is transparent that some guests with tattoos may not be permitted to use the public bath - pointing tattooed travellers to contact in advance.
stays.notes: Tattoo policy: NOT ALLOWED in public bath (explicitly stated in Expedia notes). Accepts credit cards and cashless payments - unusual for Yudanaka. Reserve public bath access in advance (contact property). Guests with tattoos should inquire about alternative bathing options.

stays.name: Airbnb Listings - Yudanaka / Yamanouchi Area
stays.name_local: エアビーアンドビー 湯田中・山ノ内エリア
stays.short_description: Private homes, kominka (old farmhouses), and apartments available via Airbnb in the broader Yudanaka / Yamanouchi area.
stays.long_description: Airbnb options in the Yamanouchi area are limited but include traditional kominka (古民家 - old Japanese farmhouse) rentals, private apartments in Nakano City (20 min drive), and occasional village houses in Yudanaka proper. These are ideal for groups or families wanting self-catering flexibility. Most Airbnb properties in this rural area do not include onsen; guests use public bathhouses (there are several in Yudanaka and Shibu Onsen villages). Tattoo policy is irrelevant for private rentals. English communication is available through the Airbnb platform with hosts.
stays.notes: Airbnb supply in this area is thin. Check listings carefully for actual Yudanaka / Yamanouchi town location vs. Nakano City. Traditional kominka properties offer authentic Japanese rural atmosphere. No onsen on-site for most - use Yudanaka public baths or day-trip onsen at Brewery Complex U.

stays.name: Yumotoya
stays.short_description: Family-oriented mid-sized ryokan with natural hot spring baths and traditional Shinshu cuisine in central Yudanaka.
stays.long_description: Yumotoya (湯元屋 - literally 'hot spring source house') is a traditional ryokan in central Yudanaka that emphasises family hospitality. The property offers communal gender-separated onsen and a kaiseki-style dinner featuring seasonal Shinshu specialties including river fish, wild mountain herbs, and local mushrooms, along with a Japanese breakfast. The name suggests the property draws directly from a natural hot spring source (yumoto). Suitable for both solo travellers and families. The property is within walking distance of Yudanaka Station.
stays.notes: Note: 'Yumotoya' (湯元屋) in Yudanaka should not be confused with 'Yumotoya' (ゆもとや) in Niigata/Iwamuro Onsen - they are completely different properties. Booking primarily via Jalan or Rakuten. Tattoo policy unconfirmed - contact property directly.

stays.name: Shiga Kogen Ski Area Accommodation (via Yudanaka as base)
stays.name_local: 志賀高原スキー場エリア宿泊
stays.short_description: Ski lodges and pensions directly on the Shiga Kogen ski area, primarily Japanese-language booking - Yudanaka is the comfortable English-accessible base town alternative.
stays.long_description: For skiers wanting ski-in/ski-out convenience, there are dozens of lodges, pensions (minshuku), and hotels directly on the Shiga Kogen plateau (1,500-2,000m elevation). These include the Hotel Grand Phenix Okushiga (luxury), Hotel Sunny Shiga (budget-friendly), and the Shiga Kogen Prince Hotel. Most are booked via Jalan or Rakuten in Japanese. The tradeoff: Shiga Kogen lodges have limited restaurant variety outside their own dining rooms, and the village atmosphere is less interesting than Yudanaka. For ski-school families or those who want to maximise slope time, on-mountain accommodation makes sense; for après-ski culture and onsen town experience, Yudanaka wins.
stays.notes: This is a category entry covering the Shiga Kogen on-mountain accommodation. For English booking, use Snow Monkey Resorts (snowmonkeyresorts.com). Shuttle buses run from Yudanaka Station to Shiga Kogen daily during ski season. Drive from Yudanaka to Hasuike gate: ~30 min on R292 (Orinpikku Kaido). Road closes for heavy snow - check conditions.

stays.name: Nakano City Hotels (Budget Gateway)
stays.short_description: Budget business hotels in Nakano City (20 min drive from Yudanaka), useful as a low-cost base with easy train access to Yudanaka Onsen.
stays.long_description: Nakano City (中野市) is the closest business-hotel town to Yudanaka, served by the same Nagano Dentetsu line. Options include Toyoko Inn, Dormy Inn, and local business hotels ranging ¥5,000-10,000/night - dramatically cheaper than Yudanaka ryokan. The train from Nakano to Yudanaka takes approximately 15-20 minutes. This option is worth considering for groups on a budget who still want to day-trip to Yudanaka's onsen and restaurants without paying ryokan rates. No onsen on-site at most Nakano business hotels.
stays.notes: Nakano Station to Yudanaka Station: ~15 min on Nagano Dentetsu. Good option for budget travellers wanting to day-trip to onsen and Snow Monkey Park. Tsuruya supermarket (ツルヤ) has a branch near Nakano for self-catering. Nakano IC on the Joshinetsu Expressway provides fast access for drivers.

stays.name: Rekishi no Yado Kanaguya
stays.short_description: The most iconic inn in Japan - a registered national cultural property whose Showa-era wooden facade is an archetype for Spirited Away.
stays.long_description: Founded around 1758 and rebuilt in glorious Showa-era timber, Kanaguya's four-storey illuminated facade on the main cobblestone street is one of the most photographed buildings in Japanese onsen culture. Corridors lit by low lanterns wind like streets between rooms, each uniquely designed. Eight natural spring baths are on-site - five private (no reservation needed, first-come), two indoor communal, and two outdoor rotenburo. A free 30-minute guided cultural tour of the building runs nightly before dinner. Kaiseki dinner and breakfast are included; rooms range from intimate 8-tatami suites to grand multi-room configurations.
amenities: 8 natural spring baths on-site (5 private, 2 indoor communal, 2 outdoor rotenburo)
Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses

stays.name: Shibu Onsen Kokuya
stays.short_description: Established 1625 and now in its 16th generation - nine indoor baths drawing from six spring sources, with private open-air rooms.
stays.long_description: Kokuya stands at the geographical and spiritual heart of Shibu Onsen, operated by the same family for nearly 400 years. The current building dates from 1957 in faithful traditional style. Six distinct spring sources feed nine indoor baths (16 tubs total) - two of which are reservable private baths - plus three outdoor rotenburo, all 100% free-flow natural spring water. Ten rooms include private open-air baths. Kaiseki meals change monthly to reflect seasonality and use Shinshu premium ingredients; guests from overseas particularly appreciate the quality. The kuyu meguri key comes with every room.
amenities: 9 indoor baths (16 tubs total) from 6 spring sources
Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses

stays.name: Senshinkan Matsuya
stays.short_description: Beloved 11-room family ryokan on the main cobbled street - warm Kodama-family hospitality, two private onsens bookable free of charge.
stays.long_description: Run by the Kodama family for generations, Senshinkan Matsuya occupies a multi-storey wooden building right on Shibu's iconic main lane. Eleven tatami rooms - some with birch trees growing through the room, an old-inn quirk beloved by guests. Two private basement onsens can be reserved at no extra charge. Breakfast is notably inventive, changing daily. Stairs are steep; not suitable for those with limited mobility. The Kodamas are known for going above and beyond - luggage delivery, restaurant tips, early check-in if possible.
amenities: 2 private basement onsens (bookable free of charge)
Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses

stays.name: Shunran no Yado Sakaeya
stays.name_local: 春蘭の宿 さかえや
stays.short_description: Top-rated ryokan in the centre of the village, with private onsen rooms, exceptional kaiseki, and a generous 15-hour stay window.
stays.long_description: Sakaeya consistently ranks among the highest-reviewed ryokan in Shibu Onsen, praised for exemplary service, exquisite kaiseki (multi-course dinners), and a notable checkout policy allowing guests to stay up to 21 hours from check-in. Rooms are traditional tatami with futon; select rooms include private outdoor baths. The staff greet guests with green tea and seasonal sweets on arrival and go out of their way to assist with local logistics. Both English and Japanese meal requests are accommodated. Colourful yukata selection is a small delight.
amenities: Indoor and outdoor communal hot spring baths
Private outdoor baths in select rooms
Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses
Kaiseki dinner and Japanese/Western breakfast included

stays.name: Furuya Ryokan (Kokuya)
stays.short_description: Note: 'Furuya' (古久屋) is the same establishment as Kokuya - the original romanization of the kanji differs by reading. See Kokuya listing.
stays.long_description: The property often listed as 'Furuya Ryokan' in English sources is the same inn as Kokuya (古久屋), a frequent transliteration variant. Founded in 1625, this 16th-generation family property remains one of Shibu Onsen's most celebrated inns. Guests receive the same nine-bath internal meguri and the public kuyu key. Please refer to the Kokuya entry for full details. When booking, confirm under the Japanese name 古久屋 or the English site at ichizaemon.com.

stays.name: Yorozuya
stays.short_description: Grand 28-room heritage inn built around 1789, with all rooms featuring private hot spring baths and a striking heritage public bath.
stays.long_description: Yorozuya is a substantial ryokan with a history stretching back to the late Edo period, now offering 28 rooms across its main building. Every room comes with its own private hot spring bath - a rare full-property commitment to in-room onsen - plus there is one additional reservable shared private bath. The public indoor baths are heritage-listed spaces. Dinner is the famous Shinshu wagyu beef, handled with a kaiseki precision that draws repeat guests. Both Japanese traditional and Western-style rooms with divan beds are available, making it one of the more accessible options for mixed-preference groups. Rated 9.4 on Expedia. A newer affiliated annex, Shoraiso (opened March 2024), offers five additional suites, all with open-air private baths.
amenities: All 28 rooms have private in-room hot spring baths
Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses
Kaiseki dinner with Shinshu wagyu beef
Station pickup (meets guests at Yudanaka Station)

stays.name: Onyado Suminoyu
stays.short_description: 12-room upscale ryokan with a 6th-floor panoramic rooftop rotenburo and Japanese-modern room interiors that suit solo travellers and couples.
stays.long_description: Suminoyu occupies a taller building than most Shibu inns, and makes excellent use of the height: the 6th-floor rooftop open-air bath offers panoramic views over the onsen town roofline to northern Shinshu mountain ranges. All-night bathing available. Rooms blend traditional tatami sensibility with modern comforts - Simmons semi-double beds in the twin rooms, kotatsu tables in tatami rooms, Bluetooth speakers, full smart toilets. Twelve rooms in total; frequently sells out. English spoken. Check-in from 1 PM, which is earlier than most ryokan in the village. Included in Rakuten Travel's recommended listings. Guests receive the kuyu key for the nine public bathhouses.
amenities: Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses
Yukata, haori jacket, geta sandals provided

stays.name: Ichinoyu Katei
stays.short_description: Intimate 11-room ryokan with a blend of three spring sources, an in-room kotatsu table, and meals served in guests' own tatami rooms.
stays.long_description: Ichinoyu Katei is a compact, characterful ryokan on Shibu Onsen's main street. The springs blend three distinct source types - guests notice the silky, warming quality that the chloride-iron combination creates. Indoor, outdoor, and private family baths are available. Notably, all meals are served in guests' rooms (traditional style), and dinner requires advance reservation (at least 3 days ahead). The free shuttle from Yudanaka Station must be booked in advance. 25 minutes by car to Shiga Kogen. Guests with visible tattoos are advised to use the private bath rather than the communal facilities.
amenities: Indoor and outdoor communal onsen baths
Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses
Kaiseki dinner and breakfast served in-room
Free shuttle from Yudanaka Station (advance booking required)

stays.name: Shibu Onsen Koishiya Ryokan
stays.short_description: Budget-smart early-Showa-era guesthouse with a renowned barista café; no private onsen, but direct kuyu key access to all nine public baths.
stays.long_description: Koishiya threads an unusual needle: a 100-year-old handcrafted wooden building now operating as a casual inn with dormitory beds, private tatami rooms, and an espresso bar that has developed a cult following. No in-building onsen - instead, guests use their kuyu key to access all nine public bathhouses on foot. No TVs or fridges in rooms; bedding is self-set. The café serves specialty-grade pour-over and espresso (closed for lunch since July 2024; open mornings and dinners). A male-only dormitory option makes it the most budget-accessible bed in the village. Shuttle to Yudanaka Station with advance booking.
amenities: Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses (no in-building onsen)
Barista café with specialty coffee (mornings and dinner service)

stays.name: Shibu Hotel
stays.short_description: Since 1935, a relaxed mid-range inn with communal, outdoor, and reservable private baths, renowned kaiseki dinner, and free stocked minibars.
stays.long_description: Shibu Hotel has been welcoming guests since 1935 and has evolved into one of the friendliest and most versatile properties in the village - not too formal, but thoroughly comfortable. Multiple bath options: communal indoor and outdoor baths, one reservable private outdoor bath, and one reservable private indoor bath. Dinner leans heavily on Shinshu ingredients; guests frequently compliment the beef. Staff have been noted for offering vegetarian kaiseki on request. Free stocked minibar in rooms is an unusual and appreciated amenity. Rated 9.8/10 on Expedia. Note: no elevator.
amenities: Communal indoor and outdoor hot spring baths
Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses

stays.name: Ozawaya Ryokan
stays.short_description: Centrally located traditional ryokan offering two types of reservable private baths and signature Shinshu wagyu-centred kaiseki meals.
stays.long_description: Ozawaya sits in the middle of Shibu Onsen's main street and is well-regarded for its Shinshu beef kaiseki - menus include Shinshu wagyu steak and Shinshu wagyu sukiyaki options as dedicated plan features. Two distinct private bath types (both exclusively rentable) give guests with tattoos a natural entry point; the tattooed-visitor community has flagged Ozawaya as one of the more accessible properties for private-bath use. Rooms are traditional Japanese style. The official website offers HP-limited pricing that undercuts OTA rates.
amenities: 2 types of reservable private baths (outdoor and indoor)
Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses
Kaiseki dinner with Shinshu wagyu beef (steak or sukiyaki plan)

stays.name: Shimaya Ryokan
stays.short_description: A small, personally run inn known for its warm host Ichiro, private onsen access by reservation, and an atmosphere of quiet authenticity.
stays.long_description: Shimaya is one of those Shibu Onsen properties that gets recommended by travellers who value personal connection over polished luxury. Run by host Ichiro and his wife, the inn is small, traditional, and unhurried. The private onsen (shared in rotation but bookable for exclusive use at a surcharge) is the main draw for guests with tattoos - it's been specifically noted by tattooed visitors as having been welcoming when privacy was arranged in advance. The cobbled main street location places guests right in the heart of village life.
amenities: Private onsen bookable for exclusive use (surcharge)
Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses

stays.name: Marukyo Ryokan
stays.short_description: Traditional small ryokan in the heart of Shibu Onsen with classic tatami rooms and kuyu key access to the nine public bathhouses.
stays.long_description: Marukyo is one of the classic mid-scale ryokan that form the backbone of Shibu Onsen's lodging landscape. Fully traditional in layout - tatami rooms, communal baths, yukata walking culture - it offers a more affordable entry into the full kuyu meguri experience. Meals are home-style kaiseki using local ingredients; the inn is small enough that service feels personal. Situated along the main cobblestone street within easy walking of all nine public bathhouses.
amenities: Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses

stays.name: Yumotoya Ryokan
stays.short_description: A long-established Shibu ryokan taking its name from the hot spring source itself - 'Yumoto' means the root of the hot water.
stays.long_description: Yumotoya (literally 'inn at the hot spring source') is one of the traditional ryokan listed on the Shibu Onsen official registry. The name references the deep connection to the spring water - Shibu Onsen's waters are among the most mineral-rich in Nagano Prefecture, and properties like Yumotoya have been built around these sources for generations. Standard tatami rooms, communal baths, kuyu meguri key access, and half-board kaiseki follow the village template. Good choice for travellers seeking an affordable, unhurried stay without the premium of flagship properties.
amenities: Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses

stays.name: Wakaba Ryokan
stays.short_description: Warmly rated small ryokan (4.7 on Ctrip) prized for attentive service; quiet and traditional in feel.
stays.long_description: Wakaba is among the smaller ryokan in Shibu Onsen, consistently noted for staff warmth and cleanliness. The name means 'young leaves', apt for a property that has a fresh, unpretentious character within an old building. Standard tatami rooms, communal baths, kuyu meguri key, and half-board kaiseki follow the Shibu template. Not to be confused with Wakabaya Shoten, the gelato shop on the main street. Good option for couples or solo travellers wanting an intimate, manageable stay.
amenities: Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses

stays.name: Onyado Hishiya Torazo
stays.short_description: Tucked beside the #9 bathhouse at the top of the village - a serene oasis known for its well-regarded baths and traditional cuisine.
stays.long_description: Hishiya Torazo occupies a quiet corner of Shibu Onsen's upper end, neighbours with Shibu-o-yu (#9 bathhouse, the largest of the nine public baths). This positioning makes it ideal for guests who want to use the public baths frequently without long cobblestone walks in geta. Small, atmospheric, and traditional - the type of inn that defines what Shibu Onsen is. Baths and cooking are frequently praised in reviews. The name, with its tiger motif (torazo), gives the property a playful character.
amenities: Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses (steps from #9 Shibu-o-yu)

stays.name: Daymaruya Ryokan
stays.name_local: 貸切露天の宿 大丸屋
stays.short_description: Owner-run budget gem with magical private outdoor onsen, husband-and-wife couple who speak excellent English and drive guests everywhere.
stays.long_description: Daymaruya is a small, family-operated inn run by a husband and wife couple who have cultivated a devoted following among international visitors. They speak excellent English and handle pickup from Yudanaka Station, drop-off at the Jigokudani Monkey Park trailhead, and general logistics with remarkable care. The private outdoor onsen - set in a quiet garden - is the property's star attraction: guests have described it as 'magical' and worth staying for alone. Three in-house onsens total. Rooms look out over the onsen street and can accommodate families. Breakfast delivered to rooms is excellent. Rated 9.1 on Booking.com. Very popular; books out quickly in ski season.
amenities: Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses
Breakfast served in-room (dinner available on request)
Free station pickup and drop-off to monkey park

stays.name: Aburaya Tousen
stays.short_description: An elegant riverside ryokan between Yudanaka and Shibu Onsen - river views, refined kaiseki, and a 10-minute drive from Shiga Highlands Roman Museum.
stays.long_description: Aburaya Tousen sits on the river between Yudanaka Onsen and Shibu Onsen, slightly outside the main village but sharing the same onsen water culture. The building overlooks the river and the resort town. Facilities include a communal bath, private outdoor bath, and a premium buffet breakfast. Rating of 4.7/5 on Jalan. Buffet breakfast and kaiseki dinner options available. It is one of the gateway-area ryokan popular with visitors to Shiga Kogen - the resort area ski drives are shorter from here than from the deepest part of Shibu village. Phone: 0269-33-3333.

stays.name: Wafu-no-Yado Masuya
stays.short_description: Beautifully decorated traditional ryokan with mountain-view rooms, excellent kaiseki, and notable warmth from staff who go the extra distance.
stays.long_description: Masuya is consistently praised by international travellers as one of Shibu's most complete ryokan experiences: rooms (smaller than average but meticulously designed), kaiseki dinners that have been called 'one of the best', and staff who provide free rides to Yudanaka Station, assist with vegetarian requests, and generally ensure guests don't feel adrift. Both indoor and outdoor onsen baths, with private reservable options. Select rooms have exceptional mountain panoramas. Two on-site restaurants.
amenities: Indoor and outdoor communal onsen baths
Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses

stays.name: Shiroganeya Ryokan
stays.name_local: 信州渋温泉 渋温泉白銀屋旅館
stays.short_description: Traditional Shibu inn on the official registry, praised for authentic Japanese atmosphere in the heart of the cobblestone district.
stays.long_description: Shiroganeya is one of the registered inns of Shibu Onsen that has drawn positive international visitor reviews for its traditional tatami rooms, genuine onsen atmosphere, and attentive hospitality. The name means 'silver house', a nod to the mercury-mineral clarity of the hot spring water. Like most Shibu properties it operates on a half-board kaiseki model with yukata walking culture built into the stay. Guests receive the kuyu meguri key on check-in.
amenities: Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses

stays.name: Minshuku Miyama
stays.short_description: Quaint minshuku near the Jigokudani trailhead - the owner couple provides translated info sheets, station pickup, and heartfelt service.
stays.long_description: Minshuku Miyama sits closer to the Jigokudani Monkey Park trailhead than the main Shibu Onsen street, making it a logical base for guests primarily visiting the snow monkeys. Run by a Japanese couple (man in his 60s, wife in the kitchen), the inn has a quietly beautiful outdoor rotenburo heated to 41°C, available to guests at no extra charge. Pre-translated information sheets in English are placed in rooms. The host drives guests from Yudanaka Station and offers a complementary transfer to the Jigokudani trailhead on departure. Kaiseki dinner with advance arrangement. This is simple, honest, Japan-at-home hospitality.
stays.address: Near Jigokudani trailhead, Yamanouchi-machi, Shimotakai-gun, Nagano
amenities: Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses
English translated info sheets in rooms

stays.name: Onyado Takamoto
stays.short_description: Traditional ryokan in the official Shibu registry - quiet, family-scale, serving the full kuyu meguri and kaiseki experience at moderate pricing.
stays.long_description: Takamoto (多喜本) is a registered ryokan in Shibu Onsen that appears in the official accommodation listing by Shibu Onsen Tourism Association. Following the village template, it offers tatami rooms, communal hot spring baths, the kuyu meguri key for the nine public baths, and half-board kaiseki. The name incorporates characters for happiness (多 = many, 喜 = joy), reflecting the traditional naming philosophy of Shibu's inns. A mid-tier option for guests who want the full onsen village experience without the premium of the flagship properties.
amenities: Kuyu meguri key for all 9 public bathhouses

stays.name: Hotel Meiko (Yomase Rising Sun Hotel)
stays.name_local: よませライジングサンホテル ホテル明幸
stays.short_description: Ski-in/ski-out hotel forming the base centre of Yomase Onsen ski resort - lift tickets, rentals and restaurants all on the ground floor.
stays.long_description: Hotel Meiko sits literally at the entrance to Mt. KOSHA Yomase Onsen ski resort: the resort's base centre 'Faro' is housed on the hotel's east side, with a rental shop, Yamazaki Y-Shop convenience store, coin lockers and lift-ticket counter. The 41-room hotel offers natural hot spring baths (Meisei-no-yu indoor daiyokujo and an outdoor bath with views over Zenkoji Plain), yukata, and full-board plans with a set-menu Japanese dinner and buffet breakfast. Restaurant La Mule also opens as a slope-side lunch spot in winter. Ski storage, coin laundry and free shuttles from Yudanaka Station are provided. The most operationally convenient base in Yomase.

stays.name: Hotel Selan
stays.name_local: よませ温泉 ホテルセラン
stays.short_description: Panoramic-view onsen hotel 2 minutes' walk from Yomase ski resort, known for spectacular sunsets over Zenkoji Plain.
stays.long_description: Hotel Selan stands at the foot of Mt. Takayashiro with sweeping views across Zenkoji Plain, the Northern Alps, and the Kita-Shiga Highlands - views good enough to earn the hotel's surroundings a place on Nagano's Sunset-Spot 100 list. The 60-room property (15 Japanese-style, 45 Japanese-Western mix) operates a large 24-hour indoor bath and two open-air baths (including a reservable private rotenburo).
